name: Puna
notes: Dry high-Andean puna (Peru, Bolivia, N Chile, NW Argentina) 3200-5000 m: bunchgrass steppe with Polylepis groves, resinous tola shrubs, Puya raimondii and hard cushion bogs (bofedales).

canopy.name: Queñua
canopy.source: Polylepis tarapacana, Bolivia/Chile/Peru/Argentina 4000-5200 m, world's highest tree, gnarled 2-8 m with peeling red bark

shrub.name: Queen of the Andes
shrub.source: Puya raimondii, Peru/Bolivia puna 3200-4800 m, giant rosette 3 m with flowering spike to 12 m, largest bromeliad

shrub.name: Puna daisy shrub
shrub.source: Parastrephia lepidophylla (tola), Bolivian/Peruvian/Chilean altiplano 3500-4800 m, resinous scale-leaved shrub 0.5-1.5 m

shrub.name: Yareta
shrub.source: Azorella compacta, Peru/Bolivia/Chile/Argentina 3200-5200 m, huge rock-hard bright green cushion mounds up to 1-3 m across

shrub.name: Puna cactus
shrub.source: Cumulopuntia boliviana, altiplano Peru/Bolivia/Chile/Argentina 3500-4700 m, spiny mound-forming cactus 10-50 cm

ground.name: Bunch grass
ground.source: Festuca orthophylla (paja brava), dominant stiff golden bunchgrass of the dry altiplano 3700-4800 m

ground.name: Ichu grass
ground.source: Jarava ichu (Stipa ichu), Peru/Bolivia/Ecuador puna 3000-4800 m, fine feathery tussock 30-100 cm

ground.name: Bofedal cushion
ground.source: Distichia muscoides, Andean peat bogs (bofedales) 3800-5000 m, hard bright-green cushion peat former

ground.name: Ground rosette
ground.source: Werneria nubigena, Peru/Bolivia puna 3800-4800 m, flat ground-hugging rosette with white daisy flowers

ground.name: Puna gentian
ground.source: Gentianella primuloides, Peruvian/Bolivian puna 3800-4600 m, tiny rosette gentian with blue-purple flowers

special.note: Catalogue plants (data/plants) whose band centres fall inside this biome's climate; computed, informational. Phase 6 may raise their density here so they are findable.

associations.name: Ichu bunchgrass puna
associations.where: wide open slopes and rolling plateaus 3800-4500 m on stony, well-drained soil
associations.source: Weberbauer 1945 El mundo vegetal de los Andes peruanos; Cabrera 1968 Ecologia vegetal de la puna (Colloquium Geographicum)

associations.name: Polylepis (quenua) woodland
associations.where: sheltered rocky slopes, boulder fields and gullies at 3800-4800 m
associations.source: Kessler 1995 Polylepis-Walder Boliviens; Fjeldsa & Kessler 1996 Conserving the biological diversity of Polylepis woodlands

associations.name: Tola shrub steppe
associations.where: dry gravelly plains and gentle slopes of the southern puna and altiplano
associations.source: Cabrera 1968; Navarro & Maldonado 2002 Geografia ecologica de Bolivia

associations.name: Bofedal cushion bog
associations.where: valley floors, spring seeps and glacier-fed flats with year-round saturated soil
associations.source: Squeo et al. 2006 Bofedales: high altitude peatlands of the central Andes (Rev. Chil. Hist. Nat.); Ruthsatz 2012

associations.name: Puya raimondii rocky slope
associations.where: steep rocky slopes and scree at 3800-4300 m among bunchgrass
associations.source: Vadillo, Suni & Cano 2004 Puya raimondii (Rev. Peru. Biol.); Weberbauer 1945
